title: Spacing between siblings only
summary: The + combinator puts a divider between items, never before the first or after the last.
explanation: .step + .step matches a .step that comes directly after another .step, which is every one except the first. A top border on those draws a line between neighbours only, with no stray line at either end.
:first-child and :last-child are the other way to do this: style everything, then undo it on the end item. The + combinator avoids the undo.
For plain spacing in a flex or grid container, gap does the same job; the sibling trick still matters for dividers and for normal block flow.
tryThis: Change .step + .step to just .step: a line appears above the first item too.
Use .step:not(:first-child) instead of .step + .step: the same result, a different selector.
Add .step:last-child { font-weight: 600; } to bold the last step.
